title: Grateful Dead Live at Carousel Ballroom on 1968-02-14
source: SBD -> (8 Track) Master Reel -> Dat -> CD -> FLAC

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear soundboard capture of a historic February 14 1968 show with smoking Dark Star/China Cat/The Eleven and an all‑time great Anthem‑of‑the‑Sun second set.
ai_review.review: The Miller soundboard source delivers remarkably crisp, balanced audio that lets the band’s 1968 peak shine through.  Highlights include a tight Dark Star → China Cat → The Eleven sequence, a flawless rendition of the Anthem of the Sun suite (Cryptical‑>The Other One, New Potato, Alligator, Caution and Spanish Jam), and powerful early versions of Morning Dew and Turn on Your Lovelight.  The performance is praised for its seamless transitions, historic significance and the band’s intense, exploratory playing.

ai_rating.rationale: Over a dozen detailed 5‑star reviews praise both the show and the recording; only one mixed 3‑star review tempers enthusiasm, yielding an overall strong rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clear mix with excellent balance; reviewers note the Miller source is superior to many official releases and captures the band’s dynamics without noticeable drop‑outs.

standout_songs: Dark Star > China Cat > The Eleven
Cryptical > The Other One (Anthem of the Sun suite)
show_quality.setlist_flow: Smooth, flawless transitions throughout both sets; the second set mirrors the Anthem of the Sun album and is highlighted for its historic sequencing and energy.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar tone is described as crisp, less snarling than on official releases, and he leads tight improvisations (e.g., Dark Star, Alligator).
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil Lesh’s bass is praised for driving the Eleven; one reviewer notes occasional flat tuning but overall solid playing.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s organ work is highlighted as a backbone on The Eleven, Alligator and the Spanish Jam; vocal presence varies.
